docs.title: Argon Wiki
docs.text:
A library mod for Palladium on Minecraft 26.1.2

Covers Argon 1.0.1

Argon helps pack developers increase what they can make. It adds abilities, conditions, render types and whole systems to Palladium, so advanced powers can be built in plain JSON without writing any Java.

Get startedAbilitiesConditionsModrinth

docs.title: What is in Argon
docs.text:
• Abilities. Energy beams (charged, cone shaped and bouncing), area bursts, ground zones, wards, domes, damage scaling and reduction, cooldown control, dispelling, cloning, possession, telekinesis, grappling, web swinging, teleporting, time control and more.
  • Conditions. Nearby entities, biome, height, sky access, health and more.
  • Effects. Bleeding, burning, freezing, shock, fear, pacified, power dampening and a few others.
  • Movement. Controlled flight with momentum and banking, directional gravity, wall crawling, charged takeoffs, and carrying entities or blocks.
  • Ability bar. A ready made bar with presets and crouch variants, so a power can have more abilities than keys.
  • Workstations. A Tech Table for crafting, modifying and customizing suit modules and accessories, a DNA transfer machine and a Chemical Synthesizer.
  • Built in documentation. Every ability and condition documents its own options in Palladium's documentation.

Argon only holds features that are not part of Palladium. Anything added to Palladium itself stays there.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: Minecraft 26.1.2 with NeoForge, Palladium 26.1.2 and Curios API. Argon does nothing on its own, so players usually install it because a pack requires it.

docs.title: Blocks
docs.text:
Block ID What it is Tech Table argon:tech_table A workbench for powered gear with Craft, Modify and Customize tabs. See the Tech Table guide. Chemical Synthesizer argon:chemical_synthesizer A machine with a 3 by 3 grid, an input tank and an output tank. It turns grid items and fluids into other fluids and items through recipes. DNA Transfer Station argon:dna_transfer_screen The control screen of the DNA Power Transfer Machine. Power Block argon:dna_transfer_power_block Supplies power to the DNA Power Transfer Machine. Chamber argon:dna_transfer_chassis The chamber a player stands in during a transfer.

The three DNA blocks are built together as one machine. See the DNA Transfer Station guide.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Every Argon command starts with /argon and needs permission level 2. Where a command takes [targets], leaving it out uses yourself.

docs.title: Grant
docs.text:
Give experience, levels or skill points to a power.

Command What it does /argon grant <targets> <power> exp <amount> Gives experience points to the power. /argon grant <targets> <power> levels <amount> Gives levels to the power. /argon grant <targets> <power> skill_points <amount> Gives skill points to the power.

docs.title: Gravity
docs.text:
Reads and changes directional gravity. See the Directional Gravity guide.

Command What it does /argon gravity get [targets] Shows the gravity direction. /argon gravity set <direction> [targets] Sets the direction. /argon gravity reset [targets] Back to normal gravity. /argon gravity strength [targets] Shows the gravity strength. /argon gravity strength <multiplier> [targets] Sets the strength multiplier. /argon gravity sources [targets] Lists what is currently changing the gravity.

docs.title: Karma
docs.text:
Reads and changes the karma of a player.

Command What it does /argon karma get <target> Shows the karma. /argon karma alignment <target> Shows the alignment it adds up to. /argon karma history <target> Shows recent karma changes. /argon karma set <targets> <amount> Sets the karma. /argon karma add <targets> <amount> Adds karma. /argon karma remove <targets> <amount> Removes karma. /argon karma reset <targets> Resets it.

docs.title: Growth
docs.text:
Reads and changes the growth stored by a Time Growth ability.

Command What it does /argon growth get <target> <power> <ability> Shows the days of growth. /argon growth set <targets> <power> <ability> <days> Sets the days. /argon growth add <targets> <power> <ability> <days> Adds days. /argon growth reset <targets> <power> <ability> Resets the growth.

docs.title: DNA vials
docs.text: Command What it does /argon dna_vial <player> <power> Gives the player a filled DNA vial of a power that is registered for the DNA Transfer Station.

docs.title: Effects
docs.text: Argon adds these status effects. Give them with /effect give <target> argon:<id>, or through an effect ability. Amplifier 0 is level I.

docs.title: Damage over time
docs.text: Effect ID What it does Burning argon:burning Sets the target visibly on fire and deals fire damage once a second: 1 plus 1 per amplifier. Does nothing to fire immune creatures. Freezing argon:freezing Builds up freezing (the powder snow effect) every tick, 4 per tick plus 4 per amplifier. Only affects creatures that can freeze. Shock argon:shock Lightning damage every 2.5 seconds: 1 plus 1 per amplifier. Sound argon:sound Sonic damage every 2 seconds (1 plus 0.5 per amplifier), 20% slower movement and flight, muted hearing, and from level III a desaturated screen. Bleeding argon:bleeding Bleed damage once a second: 1 plus 1 per amplifier, reduced by armor. Creatures in the argon:bloodless tag take none.

docs.title: Movement and control
docs.text: Effect ID What it does Slowness argon:slowness Argon's own slowness: 15% less movement speed per level, and it slows flight by the same amount. Stagger argon:stagger Slows the target. Applied by hammer hits; creatures in argon:stagger_immune ignore it and argon:stagger_reduced take less. Entrapped argon:entrapped Holds the target hovering about 1.3 blocks above the ground with no movement, flight or jumping. Restrained argon:restrained 60% less movement speed and no jumping. Restrained (boss) argon:restrained_boss The lighter version for bosses: 20% less movement speed.

docs.title: Mind effects
docs.text: Effect ID What it does Fear argon:fear Mobs run away from the source of the fear. Disoriented argon:disoriented Scrambles the movement controls. Pacified argon:pacified 15% slower attacks and 20% less damage dealt. Calmed argon:calmed Mobs with a player target drop it. Checked every quarter second. Calm Lockout argon:calm_lockout Applied by the Calm ability so it can't be used again straight away. Voiceless argon:voiceless Spellcasting mobs (the argon:spellcasters tag) lose their target and stop casting. Creatures in argon:voiceless_immune ignore it. Players can't cast by speaking.

docs.title: Attribute debuffs
docs.text: Effect ID What it does Transmuted argon:transmuted 40% smaller, 25% slower and 30% less damage. Transmuted (large) argon:transmuted_large For big creatures: 20% smaller and 15% less damage. Transmuted (boss) argon:transmuted_boss For bosses: 10% less damage. Malediction argon:malediction 25% less damage.

docs.title: Dampening
docs.text:
These switch off every power that carries the matching Palladium tag for as long as the effect lasts.

Effect ID Switches off Biological Dampening argon:dampening_biological Genetic powers Technological Dampening argon:dampening_technological Mechanical powers Mystical Dampening argon:dampening_mystical Magical powers, including spellcasting Cosmic Dampening argon:dampening_cosmic Cosmic powers

docs.title: Marker effects
docs.text:
These have no behavior of their own. Argon's abilities apply them, and conditions and other abilities can check for them.

Effect ID Used by Blessed argon:blessed The Color Cycle Glow ability Wounded argon:wounded The Ward ability and Argon's damage handling Dazzled argon:dazzled Argon's ability event handling

docs.title: Items
docs.text: Item ID What it is Structure Capsule argon:structure_capsule Holds a captured structure. Right-click a block to place the structure next to it, turned to face the way you are looking. The capsule is used up. Empty DNA Vial argon:empty_dna_vial Used at a DNA Transfer Station to take a power from a player. Filled DNA Vial argon:filled_dna_vial Holds a power. Does nothing by itself, it needs the DNA Power Transfer Machine.

docs.title: Hammers
docs.text:
Argon adds the hammer tool type, not hammers of its own. A pack makes one with the argon:hammer item type, or turns any item into a hammer with the argon:hammer data component. Hammers are heavy tools that stagger what they hit.

  • A hit applies the Stagger effect, which slows the target. Creatures in the argon:stagger_immune tag ignore it, and argon:stagger_reduced creatures are slowed less.
  • Add a pack's hammers to the argon:hammers item tag so the hammer enchantments can go on them.

docs.title: Entities
docs.text: Entity ID What it is Clone argon:clone A copy of a player made by the argon:clone ability. Thrown Block argon:thrown_block A block that has been picked up and thrown.

docs.title: Key bindings
docs.text:
All are in the Controls screen under the Argon category.

Key binding What it does Previous Ability Bar Preset Switches an argon:ability_bar to its previous preset. Next Ability Bar Preset Switches an argon:ability_bar to its next preset. Takeoff Starts a charged takeoff for the argon:charged_takeoff ability.

docs.title: Damage types
docs.text:
Damage type Death message argon:sound "was deafened to death" argon:psionic "'s mind was shattered by" argon:cosmic "was unmade by the cosmic power of" argon:shock "was electrocuted by" argon:bleeding "bled out" argon:dna_transfer "was lost in a DNA transfer"

The argon:sonic damage type tag groups minecraft:sonic_boom and argon:sound so they can be treated as one kind of damage.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
Argon ships these tags so packs can adjust its behavior by adding or removing entries.

Tag Type Purpose argon:bloodless Entity type Creatures that can't bleed. argon:spellcasters Entity type Mobs that Voiceless silences. argon:voiceless_immune Entity type Creatures Voiceless ignores. argon:pheromone_immune Entity type Creatures immune to Fear, Disoriented and Pacified. argon:stagger_immune Entity type Creatures that can't be staggered. argon:stagger_reduced Entity type Creatures staggered less. argon:karma_boss, argon:karma_dangerous, argon:karma_exempt Entity type How killing a creature changes karma. argon:beam_unmeltable Block Blocks that beams can't melt. argon:mineable/hammer Block Blocks hammers mine efficiently. argon:hammers Item Items that count as hammers. Empty until a pack adds its own.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Argon is a library mod for Palladium. It adds a large set of abilities, conditions, values, actions, beams, effects and a few machines, so addon packs can build powers without writing code. FSang18's Heroes is built on top of it.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• Minecraft 26.1.2 with NeoForge.
  • The Palladium mod. Argon needs it and does nothing without it.
  • The Argon mod file, placed in the mods folder next to Palladium.

docs.title: Using Argon in a power
docs.text:
Argon's abilities work exactly like Palladium's own. Put one in the abilities map of a power and give it a type starting with argon:.

{
  "name": "Example Power",
  "icon": "minecraft:command_block",
  "abilities": {
    "my_flight": {
      "type": "palladium:flight",
      "flight_type": {
        "type": "argon:controlled_flight",
        "profile": "natural"
      }
    }
  }
}

Argon's conditions, values and actions are used the same way, anywhere Palladium accepts a condition, a value or an action.

docs.title: How to read the reference
docs.text:
Every page in the Reference section follows the same layout:

  • ID is the value to use as type. Click it to copy it.
  • Settings lists every key with its type, what it does, whether it is required, and the fallback used when it is left out.
  • Example shows a working JSON snippet. In a power shows the same snippet inside a complete power.

Types written like Float / Value mean either a plain number or a value that changes while the game runs. A type with [] after it accepts a list.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Guides explain the bigger systems step by step.
  • Abilities and Conditions are the pages most packs use.
  • Content lists the items, blocks, effects and commands Argon adds.
  • Feature Flags explains the optional features a world or data pack has to switch on.

docs.title: Feature Flags
docs.text:
Some Argon features change how the base game or Palladium behaves, so they stay off until a pack asks for them. They are normal Minecraft feature flags, the same kind Palladium uses for its own optional features. A flag does nothing until it is enabled, so installing Argon on its own never changes an existing world.

Argon adds three flags.

Flag What it turns on argon:power_tag_parents Powers can name a tag of parent powers instead of a single parent. argon:customization/secondary_eye_selection A second set of eye pixels, picked on a Secondary tab of the eye screen. argon:customization/mouth_selection A set of mouth pixels, picked on a Mouth tab of the eye screen.

docs.title: From a data pack
docs.text:
Add the flags to the features section of the pack's pack.mcmeta. This is how FSang18's Heroes switches on Palladium's flags too.

{
  "pack": {
    "description": "My pack"
  },
  "features": {
    "enabled": [
      "argon:power_tag_parents",
      "argon:customization/secondary_eye_selection",
      "argon:customization/mouth_selection"
    ]
  }
}

A world gets the flags when it is created with the pack selected, because the flags are saved in the world's level.dat under enabled_features. Add the pack on the data pack screen of the Create World menu.

docs.title: In an existing world
docs.text: The flags a world has are stored in its level.dat under enabled_features, so a world made without the pack does not have them. The flags can be added to that list with an NBT editor while the world is closed. Make a copy of the world first.

docs.title: Power Tag Parents
Secondary Eye Selection
docs.text:
Flagargon:customization/secondary_eye_selection

Palladium's eye screen lets a player pick which pixels of the face are eyes. This flag adds a Primary and a Secondary tab to that screen, so the player can pick a second set of pixels. A pixel is either primary or secondary, never both.

  • Packs color the second set with the Secondary Eye Selection Texture (argon:eye_selection_secondary), the same way palladium:eye_selection colors the first.
  • The Reset button sends the primary pixels back to Palladium's default eyes and empties the secondary set. Save stores both.
  • The eye screen itself only appears when Palladium's own flag, palladium:customization/eye_selection, is enabled as well.

docs.title: Mouth Selection
docs.text:
Flagargon:customization/mouth_selection

Adds a Mouth tab to the same eye screen, with its own set of pixels. A pixel can be an eye, a secondary eye or a mouth, never more than one.

  • Packs color the mouth with the Mouth Selection Texture (argon:mouth_selection).
  • The mouth pixels also give beams an anchor. A beam with the body part argon:mouth starts from the mouth the player picked.
  • If both customization flags are enabled, the eye screen shows all three tabs.

The server checks the flags before it accepts a selection, so a player cannot save mouth or secondary pixels in a world that does not have the flag.

docs.title: Guides
docs.text:
Longer explanations of the bigger systems in Argon. For single abilities and conditions, use the Reference.

Controlled FlightMomentum, banking and a body that leans into its direction of travel.→ Directional GravityA gravity framework: pull a player toward any of six directions and everything follows.→ Wall CrawlingWalk on walls and ceilings, with the hitbox, camera and model following.→ Path VisionShows the holder where nearby entities and projectiles are going.→ Throwable ItemMakes any item throwable, with bounce, return, recall, homing and more.→ Tech TableTimed crafting, modules, and custom item slots, all from JSON.→ DNA Transfer StationA multiblock machine that moves powers between players and vials.→

docs.title: DNA Transfer Station (the DNA Power Transfer Machine)
docs.text: A multiblock machine that takes a Palladium superpower out of a player and into a vial, or gives a power from a vial to a player. DNA vials are only containers: they never grant anything by themselves. The machine does every transfer.

docs.title: Building it
docs.text:
Seen from the front, the machine is four blocks. All of them have to face the same way, and the Chassis can be on either side.

 [Station] [Chassis top]
 [Power ] [Chassis bottom]
Block ID What it is DNA Transfer Station argon:dna_transfer_screen The controller. Right-click for the screen. Its face shows the machine state (dark, lit, blinking), and its screen is the frame of the machine screen. Power Block argon:dna_transfer_power_block Directly under the Station. Required. Stores the RF (FE) the machine runs on; right-click it for its screen. Chamber (the Chassis in the code and below) argon:dna_transfer_chassis Two blocks high (placed like a door). The chamber the player stands in, with a sliding glass door.

The Station scans only these positions (never loads a chunk), claims the Chassis so no second Station can run it, and lets go of it when it is broken or the structure stops being valid. A transfer running at that moment is cancelled and the door opens.

docs.title: Using it
docs.text:
1. Open the door (right-click the Chassis from outside), step in. You must be inside the chamber, between its walls.
  2. Right-click the chamber wall (or the Station from outside) for the screen. Sneak and right-click inside to open or shut the door without the screen.
  3. Put a filled vial in the top slot and/or an empty vial in the bottom slot. If you have more than one power the machine can touch, pick one in the list.
  4. Shut the chamber door (the door icon on the screen, or right-click the Chamber from outside before you step in, then close it from the screen). START only works with the door shut; the status line says CLOSE THE CHAMBER DOOR TO START until it is.
  5. Press START. The door is locked for the whole transfer (100 ticks by default; nothing can open it, from inside or out), then it opens by itself. If a transfer is cancelled the door opens at once.
Vials Player has a registered power Result Empty only yes Extract: power goes into the empty vial. Filled only no Grant: the filled vial is left empty. Filled only yes Overwrite: the power they have is destroyed and replaced. Needs an explicit CONFIRM OVERWRITE every time. Filled + empty yes Exchange: their power goes into the empty vial, the new one is granted. Filled + empty no Grant (the empty vial is left alone).

Damage: 0.5 HP for each vial filled or emptied, dealt only when the transfer completes. An exchange is two. It can never take the player below half a heart.

A transfer is cancelled, changing nothing and costing nothing, if the occupant leaves, dies or disconnects, a part of the structure is removed, the energy runs out, or anything about the player or the vials differs from what was agreed when Start was pressed.

docs.title: Vials
docs.text:
• argon:empty_dna_vial, argon:filled_dna_vial.
  • A filled vial holds argon:stored_power (the power id and its liquid colour) and, for powers with persistent_data, argon:stored_power_state (that power's saved progress: level, experience, skill points, bought abilities). Filled vials do not stack, so different powers never merge.
  • Extracting with state preserved also clears the progress from the donor, so progress exists in one place only.
  • /argon dna_vial <player> <power> (permission level 2) gives a filled vial of a registered power, for testing and staff.

docs.title: Which powers the machine touches
docs.text:
The machine only ever works on powers listed in data, and only on a player's superpowers (the ones Palladium keeps in the player's superpower list: SuperpowerUtil). Suit powers, ability-given powers and anything else are never listed by it and so are never touched.

Each file in data/<namespace>/dna_transfer/powers/ can register one power, or a whole list of them in one script. It can take any of three shapes:

1. One power (an object):

{
  "power": "fsang:dc/kryptonian/absolute",
  "can_extract": true,
  "can_grant": true,
  "can_overwrite": true,
  "can_be_overwritten": true,
  "preserve_state": true,
  "display_name": { "text": "Kryptonian" },
  "colors": ["#3BF2C4", "#1B7A8C"],
  "requires": [],
  "blocked_if_holding": [],
  "energy_cost_to_start": 2000,
  "energy_cost_per_tick": 30,
  "processing_ticks": 100
}

2. An array of powers. Each item is an object like the one above, or just a power id:

[
  "mypack:mutant/regeneration",
  { "power": "mypack:mutant/telepathy", "can_overwrite": false }
]

3. An object with a powers list and a defaults area. Whatever defaults sets (the costs, or any other field below) applies to every power in the list that does not set it itself, so a pack's costs are written once and a power overrides them only if it needs to:

{
  "defaults": {
    "energy_cost_to_start": 2000,
    "energy_cost_per_tick": 30,
    "processing_ticks": 100
  },
  "powers": [
    { "power": "mypack:mutant/regeneration" },
    { "power": "mypack:mutant/telepathy", "processing_ticks": 160 },
    { "power": "mypack:cosmic/herald", "energy_cost_to_start": 8000, "energy_cost_per_tick": 80, "processing_ticks": 300 }
  ]
}

Vial colours in a script. colors is an ordinary field, so it works in defaults too: put it there for every power in the file to share, and give a power its own colors to replace it (the whole array is replaced, not merged):

{
  "defaults": { "colors": ["#3BF2C4"] },
  "powers": [
    { "power": "mypack:mutant/regeneration" },
    { "power": "mypack:mutant/telepathy", "colors": ["#B07CFF"] },
    { "power": "mypack:cosmic/herald", "colors": ["#55FF55", "#8B1A1A"] },
    { "power": "mypack:speed/force", "colors": ["#FFD83B", "#FF7A1A", "#8B1A1A"] }
  ]
}

The first power gets the default colour, the second its own single colour, the third a two-tone liquid (green on the upper left, dark red on the lower right) and the fourth three diagonal bands, yellow then orange then dark red. A power with no colour anywhere gets one picked from its id. A vial keeps the colours it was filled with, so changing a script does not recolour vials that already exist.

FSang's own powers are one script like this (data/fsang/dna_transfer/powers/fsang_powers.json). An entry that does not parse is logged and skipped; the rest of the file still loads.

All fields except power / power_tag are optional and the values above are the defaults.

Field Meaning power or power_tag The power's id, or a power tag to register many at once. An id wins over a tag. enabled false takes the power out again. Use it in a later pack to exclude a power another pack or a tag registered. can_extract May be taken out of a player and stored in an empty vial. can_grant A vial holding it may be used to give it to a player. can_overwrite When granted, it may replace a power the player already has. can_be_overwritten A player's copy may be destroyed by an overwrite (no vial to keep it). preserve_state The vial also carries the power's saved progress. Also needs the power's own persistent_data. display_name A text component to show instead of the power's own name. colors The colours of its vials' liquid: an array of one to three hex codes ("#3BF2C4", "0x3BF2C4" or "3BF2C4"; plain numbers work too). The order written is the order they are used. One colour fills the liquid. Two split it along the diagonal from its top right corner to its bottom left corner, the first on the upper left and the second on the lower right. Three cut it into three diagonal bands, the first on the upper left, the second in the middle and the third on the lower right. A lone "color": "#3BF2C4" still works as a one-entry array. By default one colour is picked from the power's id. requires Powers the player must already hold for this one to be granted. blocked_if_holding Powers that stop this one being granted while the player holds them. energy_cost_to_start Energy (FE) taken from the Power Block when a transfer of this power starts. Default: 2000. energy_cost_per_tick Energy (FE) taken every tick while it runs. Default: 30. processing_ticks How long the transfer takes, in ticks (20 = one second). Default: 100.

Whose costs a transfer uses: an extraction uses the power taken out, a grant or an overwrite the power that arrives, and an exchange (which moves both) the larger of the two for each of the three numbers.

Powers that are the parent of another power the player holds cannot be extracted or overwritten until the child is gone. A grant also has to fit Palladium's own rules (a free superpower slot, or the parent power for a child power); the machine checks this before changing anything.

Examples:

{ "power_tag": "mypack:dna_compatible" }

{ "power": "mypack:mutant/regeneration", "can_overwrite": false, "requires": ["mypack:mutant/gene"] }

{ "power": "fsang:marvel/mutant/toad", "enabled": false }

docs.title: Transfer cost
docs.text: A transfer costs 2,000 FE to start plus 30 FE a tick (5,000 FE in all over 100 ticks). A power can set its own numbers with energy_cost_to_start, energy_cost_per_tick and processing_ticks in its transfer file. Set both costs to 0 and that power needs no energy at all.

docs.title: Power Block
docs.text:
The Power Block (id argon:dna_transfer_power_block) stores the energy (FE) the machine runs on. Cables and generators can fill it from any side, and nothing can pull energy back out through them.

Right-click it for its screen: an energy bar, a charge from slot on the left (an item that holds energy, such as a battery, is emptied into the block) and a charge to slot on the right (an item that takes energy is charged from the block), up to 2,000 FE a tick each. Any item that can hold energy works, including Argon's energy items. A fuel slot in the middle burns anything a furnace burns into energy: 40 FE for every tick of the item's burn time (so a piece of coal gives 64,000 FE). It only burns while the buffer has room for the energy, so nothing is wasted.

Capacity and keeping the energy. A Power Block holds 100,000 FE by default. Capacity modules are installed from the Tech Table's Modify tab (put the Power Block in the device slot): each module adds 50,000 FE, up to 500,000 FE (eight modules). The capacity is the argon:energy_capacity component on the item, which the argon:energy_capacity modification effect changes, so the numbers live in the modification file (in FSang: data/fsang/argon/suit_modification/power_block_capacity.json, using fsang:module_capacity; copy it with your own module item for another pack). The DNA Transfer Station takes no modules.

When a Power Block is broken it drops as an item that keeps its capacity (argon:energy_capacity), the Tech Table modules recorded as installed (argon:suit_modifications, which is what the Tech Table reads back) and the energy it held (argon:energy), and placing it again gives them back. This is done by its loot table copying those three components from the block entity. The Power Block item is itself an energy item, so it can also be charged, or drained into another Power Block. The slot contents (including the fuel) drop separately, as with any container.

A transfer is paid for from this block: the start cost is taken when Start is accepted, and the per-tick cost every tick while it runs. If the buffer runs dry the transfer is cancelled and nothing changes.

docs.title: Access lock
docs.text: Public, Private (owner only), or a named player. The player who places the Station owns it. In named-player mode only that player can use the machine (the owner included, who can still change the lock to let themselves back in). Only the owner (or an operator) can change the lock. The lock stores UUIDs; names are only shown. It limits who may use the machine and never traps anyone. Clicking the access button cycles Public, Private, then the named player (once one has been set), then back to Public.

docs.title: Safety and multiplayer rules
docs.text:
• Every decision is made on the server from its own data: who is in the chamber (found from positions), what powers they hold (Palladium), what the vials hold, and whether the lock allows it. Packets from the screen are only requests and are checked again. A client cannot send a power id to be granted; the text is only compared with what the occupant really has.
  • Only the player inside the chamber can start a transfer, so nobody can strip another player from outside.
  • Both vial slots shut while a transfer runs; the door cannot be opened by hand until it ends.
  • The chamber interior is empty, so a closed door never suffocates anyone. A world reload never leaves a transfer running; it just leaves the door as it was, and the player can open it from inside.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Powers a player gets from anything other than the superpower list (suit sets, abilities) are not superpowers, so the machine leaves them alone on purpose.
  • Saved power data in a vial can be edited by anyone with creative or NBT tools. The machine caps its size (65,536 bytes) but cannot judge what is inside.
